caseno: Appeal From Appellate Decree No. 245 of 1964.
lawyer:
Md. Fazlul Karim with Mahbubey Alam ------- For the Appellants. 
Ismailuddin Sarkar ------- For Respondents No. 1, 2 & 7.
parties:
Abbas Sheikh & another ------ Defendant-Appellants. 
Vs. 
Md. Abu Hossain Sarkar and others ------Plaintiffs-Respondents.
full_judgment:
This appeal at the instance of the defendants is directed against the judgment of the lower appellate court affirming the judgment of the trial court decreeing the plaintiff's suit for declaration of title and confirmation of the possession of the disputed suit land. According to the plaintiffs the disputed jot belonged to one Kasimuddin and Imaruddin being two brothers. Imaruddin died leaving a sister and Kasimuddin. Then Kasimuddin died leaving his widow, two sons and a daughter. Then one of the sons of Kasimuddin i.e. Nurul Huq died unmarried leaving his mother, brother and sister as his heirs. One Ayenuddin predecessor of the Plaintiff Nos. 1 to 8 took settlement of the jot by a registered patta. Since the settlement Ayenuddin allegedly possessed the suit land and after his death his heirs i.e. plaintiffs had been in possession thereof within the knowledge of the defendants. The defendants No. 9 and 10 took usufructuary mortgage of the suit land from the rest of the plaintiffs and they were in possession thereof having been threatened with dispossession by the defendants, the present suit was instituted at the instance of the plaintiff for declaration of title and confirmation of possession of the suit land. 

 2. The defendants No. 1 and 6 contested the plaintiff's suit contending that Kasimuddin alone held the disputed jot under one Meharuddin by a registered kabuliyat. Imaruddin had no interest in the jot and consequently the sister of Imaruddin had no interest in the jot. Kasimuddin's widow never settled the suit land by executing any patta in favour of Ayenuddin nor did she realise any rent therefrom. The defendants were allegedly in possession of the suit land and that Ayenuddin or his successors in interest of the plaintiffs never possessed the suit land adversely to their interest within their knowledge The contesting defendant No. 1 and 6 who were respectively aged about 21 and 19 at the time of the trial of the suit were minors when the patta was executed in favour of Ayenuddin and the said patta was not binding on them and there could be no adverse possession of the suit land by dint or the said patta at least as against the contesting defendants No 1 and 6. 

 3. On consideration of the evidence on record both the courts below came to a concurrent finding of fact that the plaintiffs had acquired right, title and interest in the suit land by dint of the patta executed in favour of Ayenuddin by the sister of Imaruddin and widow of Kasimuddin who had also executed the patta on behalf on her two minor sons i.e, the present contesting defendant No. 1 and 6. With regard to the patta in question both the courts below came to a concurrent finding that by dint of the said patta the right title and interest of the sister of Imaruddin and the widow of the Kasimuddin had passed to Ayenuddin, but both the courts below also came to a concurrent finding that when the said patta was executed, minor children and on their behalf their mother i.e. the widow of Kasimuddin had executed the patta in question The court below also came to a concurrent finding that although the patta in question was partly void with regard to the right, title and interest of the defendants No. 1 and 6 since they were minors at the time of the execution of the patta and since their mother had no authority to execute the said patta on behalf of her minor children, but the plaintiffs having remained in possession of the suit land for more than 12 years, acquired right, title and interest therein by adverse possession thereof. 

 4. This case is otherwise concluded by a concurrent finding with regard to the plaintiffs' title in the suit land by dint of the patta executed in favour of the plaintiffs predecessor by the mother and aunt of contesting defendants. The only question of law raised in this case is as to whether the plaintiffs had acquired any right, title and interest in the suit land as against contesting defendant No. 1 and 6 by adverse possession of the suit land from the date of the execution of the patta when evidently the contesting defendants were minors and their mother had no authority to execute the patta on their behalf. 

 5. The learned Advocate for the defendants appellants had submitted that there—cannot be any adverse possession as against the minors during the period of their minority unless such adverse possession is claimed from the date of the attainment of their majority. The learned Advocate for the plaintiffs-respondents has, however, submitted that the suit land being jointly owned by the contesting defendants No. 1 and 6 along with their mother and aunt and the patta having been executed by the aunt and the mother not only on their own behalf but also on behalf of the minor defendants and since the plaintiffs had been in possession of the entire suit land since then, it shall be deemed that the plaintiffs had acquired right, title and interest in the suit land by adverse possession thereof. 

 6. So far the patta in question ext. 1 is concerned it was admittedly executed on 19. 12. 40. The contesting defendant No. 1 was admittedly born in 1931 and the defendant No. 2 was admittedly born in 1933. Evidently when the said patta was executed the contesting defendants were minors. The defendants No.1 attained majority in 1949 whereas the defendant No. 6 attained majority in 3951. The present suit was instituted in 1950. From the execution of the patta till the institution of the suit, the plaintiffs evident were not in adverse possession of the suit land as against the contesting defendants. As against this admitted position in fact the only question of law for consideration in this case is as to whether the plaintiffs were in adverse possession of the suit land as against the contesting defendants. As against this admitted position in fact the only question of law for consideration in this case is as to whether the plaintiffs were in adverse possession of the suit land as against the contesting defendants since the execution of the patta when they were admittedly minors.
